outcome: Interval between labor induction and delivery
cohort: The study included 94 patients with singleton term pregnancies and an unfavorable cervix (Bishop score <=6) who were not responsive to a first 24-hour dose of dinoprostone vaginal insert for labor induction.
finding: Patients who received a second dose of dinoprostone had significantly higher rates of vaginal delivery and lower rates of cesarean section compared to those treated with intravenous oxytocin.
mod_finding: A second dinoprostone vaginal insert was associated with higher vaginal delivery rates (55.3% vs 34.0%) and lower cesarean section rates (44.7% vs 66%) compared to intravenous oxytocin.
